subject: Information Theory
title: The Capacity of Wireless Channels
description: A quick, practical guide to The Capacity of Wireless Channels.

hook.text: Your phone downloads videos in seconds. The same airwaves that carried Morse code now carry gigabits.

buildup.text: Wireless capacity depends on bandwidth, SNR, and the number of independent signal paths available.

discovery.text: MIMO multiplies capacity by transmitting different data on multiple antennas simultaneously.

twist.text: Shannon's formula assumed one path. With MIMO, capacity scales with the minimum of transmit and receive antennas.

climax.text: Massive MIMO with 64+ antennas serves many users at once, approaching the theoretical limits of wireless channels.

punchline.text: More antennas, more paths, more data. Physics cooperates.

quiz.question: How does MIMO increase wireless capacity?
options: By using multiple antennas for parallel data streams
